data.title: Anthropic Is Eyeing Pricing Its IPO As High As $85 Per Share: Report
data.description:
Key points:
  • Pricing at the top of the $80 to $85 range would push Anthropic's total offering, which includes a $26 billion private placement, past $96 billion.
  • Major semiconductor firms, including Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices, have committed to purchasing shares in the private placement at the final IPO price. 
  • The company will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ‘ANT’ on Thursday.

Claude developer Anthropic PBC is weighing an initial public offering price between $80 and $85 per share, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.

The upper limit of that target range would generate as much as $70 billion from the base offering alone, according to people familiar with the internal IPO discussions quoted by Bloomberg. Combined with a separate $26 billion private placement, the total capital raised would exceed $96 billion, without expanding the number of shares available.

However, discussions are still underway and executives have not yet finalized the pricing. A representative for Anthropic did not immediately reply to Stocktwits’ request for comment.

Surpassing SpaceX

If finalized at the $85 mark, Anthropic's combined offering would surpass SpaceX's landmark debut, which raised $75 billion in its base offering and $86.2 billion after accounting for overallotment options.

Regulatory filings indicate that Anthropic previously marketed a base offering of 801.4 million shares, alongside 23.6 million shares offered by existing investors, at an initial target range of $70 to $78 per share.

Those filings also reveal that leading chipmakers, including Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD), have agreed to participate in the $26 billion private placement at the eventual IPO price.

Additionally, assuming an approximate $1.5 trillion valuation, Anthropic (ANT) would command a valuation multiple of nearly 8.5 times projected revenue, aligning its pricing with mega-cap tech giants like Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) and Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), according to New Street Research analyst Pierre Ferragu.

First Listed Frontier Lab

The debut represents a watershed moment for the technology sector, as Anthropic will become the first "frontier" AI laboratory to trade publicly, beating chief rival OpenAI, which is not expected to pursue a listing until at least 2027.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are serving as the lead underwriters for the offering, supported by a syndicate of 20 additional financial institutions. Shares of Anthropic are scheduled to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ‘ANT’.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits towards Anthropic was ‘extremely bullish’ ahead of its official pricing, with ‘extremely high’ message volumes.

data.title: StoneX Q4 EPS disappoints as net income falls 2% Y/Y
data.description:
StoneX Group stock slid 2.9% in Wednesday after-hours trading as the company's fiscal Q4 earnings failed to meet Wall Street expectations. While operating revenue grew from a year ago but fell from fiscal Q3, its expenses rose both from the prior quarter and a year ago.

Fiscal Q4 EPS of $0.66, trailing the average analyst estimate of $0.88, fell from $1.00 in Q3 and $0.70 in last year’s Q4. Net income of $84.2M fell from $127.9M in the previous quarter and $85.7M in the year-ago period.

Operating revenue of $1.46B for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, edged down from $1.47B in the prior quarter and increased from $1.20B a year ago. Net operating revenue of $655.2M, which subtracts clearing expenses, broker commissions, and interest expenses, dipped from $719.7M in Q3 and climbed from $585.1M in Q4 2025.

Operating revenue by segment:

  • Commercial rose 57% Y/Y to $466.5M
  • Institutional increased 12% Y/Y to $859.7M
  • Self-directed/retail fell 7% to $75.7M.
  • Payments grew 19% Y/Y to $62.1M.

Net contribution of $440.4M fell from $475.7M in the previous quarter and grew from $401.9M in the year-ago period.

Total fixed compensation and other expenses increased to $320.0M from $314.2M in Q3 and $293.8M in last year’s Q4.

Adjusted EBITDA of $193.7M compared with $229.5M in the prior quarter and $170.9M a year ago.

Return on equity was 11.6%, down from $18.4% in the previous quarter and 15.2% a year ago.

Conference  call on Nov. 19 at 9:00 AM ET.

data.title: Has the stock market's correction hit bottom yet? Here's what these contrarian indicators say.
data.description:
By Mark Hulbert

Contrarian buy signals typically don't come until sentiment has dropped further than they have so far

We're not at the bottom yet, it appears.

The bottom of the stock market's correction is still ahead of us, according to contrarian analysis.

That surprises some traders, since the stock market's recent declines and extraordinary volatility has caused the mood on Wall Street to sour. Surely the veritable Wall of Worry that markets like to climb has been sufficiently rebuilt?

No, according to my auditing firm's monitoring of short-term market timers. Though it is true that they are less bullish than they were six weeks ago, they have not yet become bearish enough to satisfy contrarians' criteria for a buy signal.

Consider these timers' average recommended equity exposure level. The Hulbert Stock Newsletter Sentiment Index (HSNSI), which reflects this average among several dozen short-term market timers who focus on the broad stock market. As you can see from the accompanying chart, it has declined to just the upper edge of the excessively bearish zone that I have used in prior columns about market sentiment. That zone is defined as the range of readings in the bottom decile of the historical distribution.

Contrarian buy signals typically don't come until sentiment has dropped further into that zone and stays there for a number of trading sessions.

An even stronger indication that a buy signal would be premature comes from the Hulbert Nasdaq Newsletter Sentiment Index (HNNSI), which is a similar sentiment measure except that it includes a different group of timers - those who focus on the Nasdaq market in particular. (This second index is not in the accompanying chart.) This index has dropped even less than the HSNSI, which is surprising since the Nasdaq market has suffered significantly more in recent weeks than the broad market. While the S&P 500 SPX is 6.3% below its early October high, for example, the Nasdaq Composite COMP is 11.5% below.

Other sentiment measures are also suggesting that the decline has further to go. Consider the weekly sentiment survey that the American Association of Individual Investors conducts of its members. Those who say they are bullish, expressed as a percentage of those who are either bullish or bearish, just this week dipped to the upper end of what I have defined as the excessively bearish zone. The VIX VIX (Cboe's Volatility Index, aka the investor-fear index) is currently pointing away from being in its excessively bearish zone.

Surging demand for Anthropic's upcoming IPO provides yet more evidence of these pockets of bullishness. The company's IPO reportedly has been nearly seven times oversubscribed.

The bottom line: Sentiment is moving in the right direction to entice contrarians to declare that a tradable bottom is in. But it's not there yet.

Mark Hulbert is a regular contributor to MarketWatch. His Hulbert Ratings tracks investment newsletters that pay a flat fee to be audited. He can be reached at mark@hulbertratings.com

-Mark Hulbert

Revenue increased by $0.5 million, or 19%, compared to the same period last year. The increase reflects greater tipping fee revenue from higher volumes at the organic waste and composting facilities and stronger RNG output at the Fraser Valley Biogas (“FVB”) and Grow the Energy Circle (“GrowTEC”) facilities.

The net loss decreased by $0.4 million, or 40%, compared to the same period last year, driven by revenue growth, absence of loss on sale of assets, partially offset by higher general and administrative expenses.

Adjusted EBITDA increased by $0.5 million, or 99%, year over year, supported by higher tipping volumes at the organic waste and composting facilities and greater RNG production and related revenue at FVB and GrowTEC.

RNG output reached 56,064 GJ, an increase of 8% over Q3 2025, as the FVB and GrowTEC RNG facilities continued to operate at more stable levels.

Subsequent Events

Subsequent to quarter-end, Farm Credit Canada (“FCC”) expanded its existing project-level credit facility at the Company’s Fraser Valley Biogas facility by $0.8 million. The additional funding will finance near-term optimization at FVB, with the replacement of the facility’s thermal oxidizer, a part of the biogas upgrading process, with a new, more energy-efficient unit.

The upgrade has a total estimated capital cost of approximately $1.4 million, to be funded by a combination of proceeds from this FCC facility increase and operating cash flow. EverGen anticipates partially offsetting these costs by applying for rebates under FortisBC’s Custom Efficiency Program once the upgrade is complete and the actual energy savings are confirmed. The new unit is targeted to be operational by mid-2027. With FVB and GrowTEC continuing to set new RNG production records, the upgrade is expected to further improve efficiency at FVB and support stronger cash flow from EverGen’s core operating assets.

Management Commentary

“Our third-quarter results show our operating improvements continuing to pay off, with higher RNG output and growing feedstock volumes,” said Chase Edgelow, Co-founder and CEO of EverGen.

“With our core assets performing steadily and the Pacific Coast Renewables RNG expansion progressing towards a final investment decision, we remain focused on disciplined capital allocation and accretive growth across both our existing development pipeline and selective inorganic opportunities.

“The increased FCC facility supports a short-payback optimization project at FVB that we expect will improve energy efficiency and cash generation once complete. Pairing low-cost, non-dilutive project-level debt with available grants and incentives is a repeatable playbook we can apply to growth and optimization across the portfolio.”

Complete details of the quarter’s results are available in the Company’s Consolidated Financial Statements and Management’s Discussion and Analysis, which can be found on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the EverGen website at www.evergeninfra.com.

About EverGen Infrastructure Corp.

EverGen, Canada’s Renewable Natural Gas Infrastructure Platform, is combating climate change and helping communities contribute to a sustainable future. Headquartered on the West Coast of Canada, EverGen is an established independent renewable energy producer which acquires, develops, builds, owns, and operates a portfolio of Renewable Natural Gas, waste-to-energy, and related infrastructure projects. EverGen is focused on Canada, with continued growth expected across other regions in North America and beyond.

For more information about EverGen Infrastructure Corp. and our projects, please visit www.evergeninfra.com.

Non-GAAP Measures

EverGen uses certain financial measures referred to in this press release to quantify its results that are not prescribed by IFRS Accounting Standards. The terms EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA and working capital are not recognized measures under IFRS Accounting Standards and may not be comparable to that reported by other companies. EverGen believes that, in addition to measures prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards, the non-GAAP measurement provides useful information to evaluate the Company’s performance and ability to generate cash, profitability and meet financial commitments. These non-GAAP measures are intended to provide additional information and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for other measures of performance prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards. EBITDA is defined as net income (loss) before interest, tax and depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is EBITDA adjusted for share-based payment expenses, certain non-cash items, unusual or non-recurring items, contingent consideration gains and losses and non-controlling interests in adjusted EBITDA. data.description:
EverGen reported Q3 2026 revenue up $0.5M, or 19%, and net loss down $0.4M, or 40%, year over year. Adjusted EBITDA rose $0.5M, or 99%, and RNG output increased 8% to 56,064 GJ; FCC expanded its FVB credit facility by $0.8M.

Material Details

#DetailAI Analyst View
1Revenue rose $0.5M, or 19%, year over yearGrowth was attributed to higher tipping-fee revenue and stronger RNG output, indicating improved operating activity.
2Adjusted EBITDA rose $0.5M, or 99%, year over yearThe sharp increase signals better operating performance; the release provides no absolute EBITDA figure.
3Net loss fell $0.4M, or 40%, year over yearLosses narrowed, partly due to the absence of a prior-period asset-sale loss; higher G&A partly offset the improvement.
4RNG output rose 8% to 56,064 GJHigher production supports revenue growth; the comparison is with Q3 2025.
5FCC facility increased by $0.8M for FVBProject-level funding supports the near-term upgrade, but adds debt and is not company-wide unrestricted financing.
6Oxidizer upgrade costs approx. $1.4M; target mid-2027The planned efficiency project requires operating cash flow alongside facility funding; rebates are only an application anticipated after completion.

Context by AI Analyst

The results indicate continuing operating improvement at EverGen’s existing RNG and waste facilities, rather than a new growth-cycle inflection. Further upside depends on completing the FVB upgrade by its mid-2027 target and demonstrating energy savings, while the Pacific Coast Renewables expansion would need to reach a final investment decision.

Based on the original press release from EverGen Infrastructure Corp. distributed by BusinessWire.

data.title: Nasdaq Regains Ground Despite Nvidia Slump But Dow Tumbles To Five-Month Closing Low
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After trending lower over the past several sessions, stocks turned in a relatively lackluster performance during trading on Wednesday. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 spent much of the day lingering near the unchanged line, although the narrower Dow showed a notable move to the downside.

The major averages eventually ended the day mixed. While the Nasdaq climbed 101.50 points or 0.4 percent to 24,429.88, the S&P 500 dipped 16.90 points or 0.2 percent to a three-month closing low of 7,323.63.

The Dow slumped 561.25 points or 1.1 percent to 50,198.17, hitting its lowest closing level in five months amid a 10.2 percent nosedive by shares of UnitedHealth (UNH).

The choppy trading on Wall Street came as traders digested highly anticipated earnings news from AI giant and market leader Nvidia (NVDA).

After seeing pre-market strength, shares of Nvidia tumbled by 2.9 percent to their lowest closing level in over a year even though the company reported better than expected fiscal third quarter results and raised its revenue guidance.

'Elements of the company's results clearly haven't stood up to greater scrutiny despite upgraded guidance and better-than-expected numbers,' said AJ Bell head of markets Dan Coatsworth. 'While revenues are continuing to grow at pace, there is clearly some concern about how this growth is being financed and how it is converting into profit and cash flow.'

He added, 'Investors are less minded to give the business the benefit of the doubt in the wake of the messy departure of former CEO Jensen Huang, and the shares are now on the verge of testing 52-week lows once more.

Traders may also have been reluctant to make more significant moves ahead of Claude developer Anthropic's initial public offering later this week.

'Anthropic offers the next test of appetite with its IPO is expected to be priced today, ahead of an anticipated Nasdaq debut tomorrow,' said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com.

'Strong demand and a firm first day of trading would suggest investors remain willing to back AI growth, even if they are becoming more selective,' she added. 'A weak reception would add weight to concerns that expectations across the sector have run ahead of what investors are prepared to pay.'

Sector News

Despite the lackluster performance by the broader markets, gold stocks showed a substantial move to the downside amid a steep drop by the price of the precious metal.

With U.S. gold futures plunging by 3.5 percent to their lowest levels in a year, the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index nosedived by 5.6 percent to a three-month closing low.

A significant decrease by the price of crude oil also weighed on oil producer stocks, with the NYSE Arca Oil Index plummeting by 4.3 percent.

Pharmaceutical, healthcare and banking stocks also saw considerable weakness, while networking and retail stocks showed strong moves to the upside.

Other Markets

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region turned in a mixed performance during trading on Wednesday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index rose by 0.3 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index slid by 0.9 percent.

Meanwhile, the major European markets all moved to the downside on the day. While the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index tumbled by 1.3 percent, the German DAX Index slumped by 1.2 percent and the French CAC 40 Index declined by 0.9 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries have extended the upward move seen over the two previous sessions. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has fallen 3.5 basis points to 5.068 percent.

data.title: MVB Financial Corp. Declares Fourth Quarter 2026 Dividend
data.description:
MVB Financial Corp. () (“MVB” or the “Company”) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.17 per share, consistent with the previous quarter’s dividend. The dividend is payable on December 15, 2026, for shareholders of record as of December 1, 2026. This is the fourth quarterly dividend for 2026.

“During the third quarter, MVB made tangible progress on several key initiatives that are strengthening our underlying business. Net interest income increased 18% through the first nine months of the year, while core net interest margin expanded by 15 basis points during the quarter to 4.02%. An important contributor to that improvement has been the continued growth of our Fintech Payments deposit relationships. Our payments business is also generating meaningful fee income growth, with payment card and service charge income up 22% through the first nine months of the year. Quarterly noninterest expense declined below $30 million, reflecting continued expense discipline. We believe our progress in funding diversification, payments revenue growth and operating efficiency is strengthening the foundation for improved financial performance,” said Larry F. Mazza, President and Chief Executive Officer, MVB Financial.

About MVB Financial Corp.

MVB Financial Corp. () is an innovative bank powering Fintech solutions in payments, card issuance and online gaming programs for leading Fintech companies nationwide, while providing traditional retail and commercial banking services within established markets. MVB’s comprehensive platform includes money movement solutions across all modalities and embedded finance capabilities. MVB combines proven Fintech builder/incubator capabilities, innovative culture, regulatory expertise, core banking and AI-driven operational efficiency to enable Fintech partners to navigate complex regulatory requirements while accelerating time-to-market.

For more information about MVB, please visit https://ir.mvbbanking.com.
